variants.name: Current architecture
variants.summary: Service level: Codex integration inside the Archboard server. Follow linked subjects for related levels.

nodes.name: Agent workbench
nodes.responsibility: Everything archboard owns around one private Codex child, inside the Archboard server
nodes.description: Not a deployment of its own: this lives in the Archboard server process. The Codex app-server is its child.

nodes.name: Generation composition
nodes.responsibility: Starts the private child, then builds each generation's object graph over a transport and identity ledger that outlive it
nodes.description: installProductionCodexWorkbench hands the owner lifecycle createCodexProcess and a generation factory; the factories (codex-workbench-factories.ts) build the components in the order they depend on each other, the gateway last.

nodes.name: Browser gateway
nodes.responsibility: The one door a browser has into the workbench: snapshots out, admitted commands in, one lease at a time

nodes.name: Codex process
nodes.responsibility: Owns the child: proves the executable, prepares the Codex home every Archboard server on the machine shares, spawns the child and reaps its group
nodes.description: One Archboard-only CODEX_HOME and SQLite home under the state directory serve every server on the machine, so one sign-in serves them all; each server keeps its own owner lock and epoch ledger under its port. Its config.toml gets the auto-review defaults it lacks (approvals_reviewer auto_review, workspace-write sandbox with network access) and keeps whatever Codex or a person set; a config naming another SQLite home, or not TOML, is refused.

nodes.name: Codex transport
nodes.responsibility: One newline-framed JSON object at a time each way, correlated to its request, and each tool call routed to the owner registered for its namespace
nodes.description: The versioned wire contract it decodes against lives beside it in codex-protocol. A dynamic tool call reaches the owner registered for its namespace and manifest digest: the thread tools, the coordinator tools, or tell_coordinator.

nodes.name: Codex session
nodes.responsibility: One initialized session and the reviewed methods it will send

nodes.name: Thread link
nodes.responsibility: Which thread the Archboard server is bound to, made by the first message or Talk: the candidates, the binding, and the refusal when two disagree

nodes.name: Workhorse queue
nodes.responsibility: Codex's queue of messages waiting for the workhorse: list, add, edit, reorder, delete, or start one now

nodes.name: Voice coordinator
nodes.responsibility: The separate fast thread voice attaches to, the voice model's subconscious, which routes sustained work to the workhorse

nodes.name: Codex app-server
nodes.responsibility: The Codex binary, run as one private child over stdio in the Archboard-only Codex home
nodes.description: Spawned as `app-server --stdio --strict-config`. Its threads are the workhorse and the coordinator, and every thread runs in its auto-review mode; nothing here describes its internals.

nodes.name: Browser pane
nodes.responsibility: The pane a user works in: it holds the lease, sends commands and draws the published state

nodes.name: Epoch ledger
nodes.responsibility: Which child generation owns which thread, on disk, with staged operations that commit or roll back

nodes.name: Workhorse operations
nodes.responsibility: The four things the coordinator may ask of a workhorse, one at a time: delegate, steer, inspect, manage its queue

nodes.name: Realtime voice
nodes.responsibility: Starts the realtime leg on the coordinator's thread, hands a narrated walkthrough's steps to the voice model, and carries its transcript back
nodes.description: Archboard never speaks to a voice endpoint itself: the child brokers it, and the media travels browser to provider over the peer connection the tab made.

nodes.name: Approvals
nodes.responsibility: Every approval the child raises: staged, published once, answered exactly once, settled

nodes.name: Thread tool calls
nodes.responsibility: The archboard_app tools a thread calls on the server's other threads: list, read, create, fork, message, wait
nodes.description: A creation, fork or message runs only once the user approves it in the pane, under the generation that may act.

nodes.name: Coordinator callbacks
nodes.responsibility: While voice is live, workhorse news for the coordinator and pane news for the voice model, each once and in order

nodes.name: Board-change delivery
nodes.responsibility: Tells the linked workhorse what a user changed on a board: one quiet developer message, settled once
nodes.description: Before each delivery it checks the child, epoch, thread link and cursor again; the outcome is delivered, not delivered with a reason, or unknown, and it is never retried.

nodes.name: Semantic context
nodes.responsibility: Turns a user's gestures and settled board changes into briefs and events for whoever subscribes

beats.heading: A private child, composed once
beats.body: The workbench proves the executable and prepares an Archboard-only Codex home that every Archboard server on the machine shares, so one sign-in serves them all; it fills in the auto-review defaults its config.toml lacks and keeps what Codex or a person set. The owner lock and epoch ledger are the server's own. Then it starts the child and builds one generation's parts in the order they depend on each other.

beats.heading: Only reviewed methods reach the wire
beats.body: The session publishes the methods that have been reviewed against the pinned contract, and the transport carries one framed object at a time each way. A reply that does not decode is a refusal, not a guess.

beats.heading: The server holds the link; a pane holds the lease
beats.body: The Archboard server's thread link names one workhorse, whichever pane speaks. The pane holding the lease sends its typed message straight to that thread as a turn or a steer, and edits the thread's queue. The coordinator's work goes through the four operations instead, each staged in the epoch ledger so a child that dies mid-flight leaves a stated outcome rather than a guess.

beats.heading: Voice is a separate thread, not a second mouth
beats.body: The coordinator is its own thread with its own model and settings, and the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorse and decides what the voice model says, and it runs only while voice is live. It does bounded work itself and routes anything sustained to the workhorse through the four operations.

beats.heading: The coordinator hears the workhorse at once
beats.body: While voice is live, a workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator, reaches the coordinator as one sentence in a turn/start: Codex adds it to the coordinator's running turn or starts one. With no voice session, or while a recording holds the voice, nothing is sent.

beats.heading: Board changes reach the workhorse quietly
beats.body: A settled change a user made is injected into the linked workhorse's history as one developer message, after the child, epoch, link and cursor are checked again, and starts no turn. It settles once as delivered, not delivered or unknown, and is never retried or sent anywhere else.
